findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: In packages/core/EventManager.ts line 119 the code does const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null, undefined or [], the destructured variable is undefined and accessing .integration throws TypeError. Previously evt.destinationCalendar?.integration was safe. Consequence: any booking/create without a destination calendar crashes event creation and falls back from Google Meet to Cal Video check never runs.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback calendar is dead code
findings.body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 254-256 selectedCalendar is externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. The else branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but then it searches for cal.externalId === externalCalendarId which can never match, so it always yields undefined. Previously it fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Consequence: updates without externalCalendarId call Google with calendarId undefined and fail.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback calendar is dead code
findings.body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 315-317 calendarId is externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. The else branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy and therefore the find predicate never matches, yielding undefined and falling back to primary. Previously it fell back to the stored destinationCalendar. Consequence: deletions for old bookings without externalCalendarId delete from wrong calendar or silently miss.

findings.title: patch uses undefined calendarId after primary fallback
findings.body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 168 calendar.events.patch uses calendarId: selectedCalendar while insert uses calendarId: selectedCalendar || primary. When no destination matches credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined, insert goes to primary but patch is called with undefined. Consequence: Google patch call fails or throws after successful insert when hangoutLink is present.

findings.title: Collective second host gets first host organizer email
findings.body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 100-103 and 122-124 mainHostDestinationCalendar is always element 0 of destinationCalendar and its externalId is used as organizer email for every create/update. EventManager now loops over each destination and calls createEvent per credentialId, but the payload still uses the first host calendar. Consequence: events created in the second host calendar carry the first host email as organizer, causing wrong invites and ownership.

findings.title: Required credentialId breaks Calendar interface
findings.body: In packages/types/Calendar.d.ts line 221 createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number) makes the second argument required, while Lark, Office365 and BaseCalendarService still implement createEvent(event) with one param and other callers may call with one arg. In TypeScript implementations with fewer params are allowed but callers with one arg now fail type checking. Consequence: breaking contract change; it should be credentialId?: number to remain backward compatible.

findings.title: Collective destinations lost when organizer has no calendar
findings.body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a calendar, then code does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) for COLLECTIVE. When it is null the optional push is a no-op. Consequence: for collective events without organizer destination, team host calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are silently dropped and hosts never get calendar invites.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancel only deletes organizer calendars
findings.body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts lines 449-461 the allRemainingBookings recurring path iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials to delete updatedBookings references. For collective bookings other hosts credentials and calendars are not in that user object. Consequence: cancelling all recurring instances leaves orphan events on co-host calendars.
